title: Base change of a module along a ring map
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $M$ an $R$-module. The *base change* (extension of scalars) of $M$ to $A$ is the tensor product $M\otimes_RA$, an $A$-module by $a\cdot(m\otimes b)=m\otimes ab$, with the $R$-linear map $M\to M\otimes_RA$, $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. An $R$-linear map $f:M\to N$ induces the $A$-linear map $f\otimes_RA:M\otimes_RA\to N\otimes_RA$, $m\otimes b\mapsto f(m)\otimes b$, and $f\mapsto f\otimes_RA$ is $R$-linear and compatible with composition and identities. An $R$-bilinear map $\beta:M\times N\to P$ induces the unique $A$-bilinear map $\beta_A:(M\otimes_RA)\times(N\otimes_RA)\to P\otimes_RA$ with $\beta_A(m\otimes a,n\otimes b)=\beta(m,n)\otimes ab$.
